extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, licensees, and IP practitioners (Turkey)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria and standards from Turkish patent legislation covering compulsory licensing, invalidity, termination, infringement, utility models, procedures, remedies, and compensation. Useful for practitioners advising on patent rights, enforcement, and administrative procedures in Turkey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and grounds for requesting compulsory license for non-use
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three years after grant decision related to a patent is published in the Bulletin or within four years after date of patent application, whichever expires later, a relevant person may request a compulsory license on grounds that the invention wasn’t started to be used or serious and real initiatives haven’t been made for use or use was not at level to meet national market needs; repeated breaks in use more than three years without justifiable reason are also grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request may be made as from date of expiration of that period. The provisions specify both temporal windows (3 years after publication of grant decision or 4 years after filing, whichever later) and substantive use/market-supply grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license because of dependency between patents
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is not possible to use a later-dated patent without infringing an earlier patent, dependency arises; the owner of the later patent cannot use the invention covered by the earlier patent without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner of the later-dated patent may request a compulsory license if the later invention produces a significant technical advancement providing largely economic benefits. If granted to the later patentee, the earlier patentee may likewise request a compulsory license to use the later patent. If one dependent patent becomes void or expires, the compulsory licensing decision is eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license in the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory license may be granted where use, increased use, dissemination, or improvement of an invention is of great importance for public health or national security, or where non-use/insufficient use would cause serious damage to economic or technological development; decision by Council of Ministers upon ministry proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-interest compulsory licenses may be exclusive and may be limited to one or more businesses, especially for national security. For public health/national security cases, the relevant ministry must obtain approvals (e.g., from Ministry of National Defense or Ministry of Health).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal nature and conditionality of compulsory licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory license is generally non-exclusive, but licenses granted for public interest may be exclusive. Licenses are granted under certain conditions considering time, fee and area of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts consider the economic value of the patent in setting license fees. For compulsory licenses under public-interest import provisions, economic value in terms of the importing country, non-commercial and humanitarian purposes are to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on licensee rights (sub-licensing and importation)
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of a compulsory license, the licensee has no right to grant sublicenses or import the subject of the patent, except where compulsory license granted because of public interest explicitly authorizes importation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Import authorization for public-interest compulsory licenses is limited in quantity and time. If trust relationship between patentee and licensee is violated because of the compulsory license, the licensee may request a discount from the license fee proportional to the violation's effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of compulsory license with respect to additional patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory license includes the supplements (additional patents) of existing patent on the date of acceptance of the license; licensee may request that later-granted patents serving the same use be included in scope of compulsory license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parties disagree on fees or conditions due to additional patents, the court determines them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer rules for compulsory licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory license shall be transferred in conjunction with the business or part of business where the license is exercised to ensure transfer validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compulsory license is granted due to dependency, the license transfers together with the dependent patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change and cancellation of compulsory license conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: After a compulsory license is granted, the licensee or patent holder may request the court to change the fee or conditions based on subsequent events; court may cancel license upon patent owner request if licensee seriously or continuously breaches obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court also cancels license when conditions that justified granting end and recurrence becomes impossible. Parties may seek contractual licensing under more favorable terms to support a change request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of contractual license provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Articles 126-136, contractual license provisions stated in Article 125 and Article 126 apply to contractual and compulsory licenses as well, insofar as they are not contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractual terms may supplement statutory compulsory license provisions unless they conflict with mandatory rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for invalidity of a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Office’s final decision, a patent may be declared invalid if: (a) subject lacks patentability per Articles 82 and 83; (b) invention not sufficiently explained per Article 92; (c) subject exceeds scope of first application or first version of first application (including divisional bases); (ç) patent owner lacks right to demand patent under Article 109; (d) extent of protection is exceeded and court decides invalidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidity can be decided following the Office's final decision; various statutory articles are referenced for specific standards on novelty, inventive step, sufficiency of disclosure and entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural limits on invalidity requests prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to publication made per specified paragraphs of Article 99, the court shall not decide invalidity requests made pursuant to certain grounds (subparagraphs (a), (b), (c) of first paragraph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that the patent owner does not have right under Article 109 may be alleged only by the holder of the invention or successors. The invalidity proceeding may be instituted against those registered as owner during protection or within five years following termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial invalidity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If causes of invalidity relate only to part of a patent, the claims related solely to that part shall be cancelled and partial invalidity of the patent decided. Partial invalidity for a claim shall not be decided. If an independent claim is revoked, dependent claims that lack patentability on their own are also revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If remaining claims comply with patentability conditions, the patent remains valid for those parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and retroactivity of invalidation decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is decided invalid, the decision takes effect retroactively and the protection is deemed null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions preserve (a) final decisions given and implemented due to infringement prior to the invalidity decision, and (b) contracts concluded and implemented prior to the invalidity decision. Parties may seek equitable partial or full return of paid price under existing contracts. Final invalidity decisions bind everyone; Office will cancel and publish revocation in the register/Bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedures for termination of patent right
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent right terminates upon: (a) expiry of protection period; (b) waiver by patent holder; (c) failure to pay annual fee within specified periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office publishes termination. Subject matter of a terminated patent belongs to the public from execution date. Waiver can be partial (one or more claims) but requires notification to Office, is effective from registry record date, and sometimes requires permission of registered right/license holders or third parties with interlocutory injunctions. Waiver decisions are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts deemed as infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement includes: (a) partially or completely imitating the patented product resulting from production without consent; (b) selling, distributing, releasing commercially, importing, keeping for commercial purposes, making available, or proposing contracts related to such products when it is known or required to be known they are produced by imitation; (c) using a patented method without consent or selling/distributing products directly produced by such method similarly; (ç) usurping patent rights or expanding rights granted by contractual or compulsory license without permission or transferring them to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute lists production, commercialization, distribution, use of patented methods, and unlawful expansion/transfer of granted rights as infringing acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary rule for method-related patents and product presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is for a method of obtaining a product/material, the court may require the defendant to prove that the defendant’s method is different. If the product/material obtained by the patented method is new, the same product/material produced without permission is deemed to have been obtained by the patented method; the defendant must prove otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legitimate interests of the defendant (e.g., protecting production and business secrets) must be considered when the defendant is required to disclose evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and effect of publication of application
rubrics_metrics.description: From the date of publication of a patent or utility model application, the applicant is authorized to institute legal proceedings for infringements. If an infringer was informed about the application, whether the application is published is immaterial. If the court finds malicious intent by the infringer, infringement may be accepted as occurring prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to certain publications, the court shall not decide on validity of claims; publication affects standing to sue and evidentiary timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model eligibility and excluded subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility models protect inventions which are new under Article 83 and industrially applicable; technical specifications not contributing to the subject of the invention are disregarded in innovation evaluation. Exclusions: chemical/biological substances or methods, pharmaceutical substances or methods, biotechnological inventions, and products obtained by such methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law lists specific categories excluded from utility model protection; examiners disregard non-contributing technical details when assessing innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model procedural requirements (formal exam, search, corrections, grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: If application lacks elements of Article 90(3) it is not processed. Deficiencies (including foreign-language elements) must be corrected within two months or application is deemed withdrawn. Applicant must demand search within two months of notification of formality consistency or correction; a search report is issued and published. If subject falls into excluded types or description/claims unclear, no search report is prepared and applicant must file objections or changes within three months or be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can appeal search report contents within three months from its publication; third parties may present opinions. If Office decides to grant, decision and utility model are published. Amendments requested as condition of grant must be fulfilled within two months. After granting, appeals per Article 99 are not available; only invalidation actions before court. Granting is not a guarantee of validity or usefulness; implementing principles are set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of utility model (grounds and parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may accept invalidation of utility model if it does not meet Article 142 conditions, the invention isn’t sufficiently explained per Article 92, subject exceeds scope of first application/version, or owner lacks right under Article 109. Those with interests, public prosecutors or relevant institutions may demand invalidation; if owner lacks right per Article 109 only the holder of the invention or successors may do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation proceedings may be instituted against registered owners during protection or within five years after termination; partial invalidity rules mirror those for patents. The same rules on who may allege entitlement apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of patent provisions to utility models and prohibition on double protection
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no clear provision related to utility model and nothing contradicts utility model nature, patent provisions apply to utility models. The same person (or successor) shall not be granted more than one patent or utility model or any two independently about the same invention in the same scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents double protection of the same subject matter under patent and utility model systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods and notifications for Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Period to be observed in all actions related to industrial property rights before the Office, including appeals, is two months from notification date unless specified otherwise in the Code or regulation. Failure to obey these periods means the demand is deemed not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general deadline rule applying across Office proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint representative rules for multiple right holders
rubrics_metrics.description: If industrial property right belongs to more than one person and no representative has been assigned, all operations before the Office (except withdrawal/waiver) are carried out by the right owner appointed as joint representative by the right holders; if none appointed, the first right holder mentioned in the application form is deemed joint representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the joint representative's domicile is outside Turkey, operations must be carried out by a trademark or patent attorney. Collective trademark provisions reserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability and formal requirements for legal actions on industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property rights may be transferred, inherited, licensed, pledged, shown as collateral, seized or become subject of other legal actions. Legal actions shall be in writing and transfer contracts valid only if notarized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights arising from legal actions may be registered and published in the Bulletin upon request and payment; unregistered rights may not be enforced against third parties acting in good faith. Geographical indications and traditional product names are excluded from license/transfer/inheritance/confiscation and use as collateral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-emption right of co-owners on sale of share
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is more than one owner of an industrial property right, other stakeholders have pre-emption right when any owner sells its share partly or wholly to a third party; sale must be reported; pre-emption right lapses after three months from notification or in any case after two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parties cannot agree, the pre-emption right can be exercised by litigating against buyer; buyer/seller must report sale. Pre-emption is void in forced sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available claims/remedies for right owners in infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Right owner may claim: determination of infringement existence; prevention of possible infringement; stopping infringing actions; remedy and compensation for material and moral damages; seizure of infringing products and instruments exclusively used in their production; being granted property right on seized items; measures to prevent continuity of infringement including altering shapes, erasing trademarks, or destroying items; and announcement of final judgment at infringer's expense when justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value of seized devices/machines is deducted from compensation; if value exceeds compensation, excess paid to opposing party. Announcement scope and form determined in the ruling; claim for announcement must be made within three months after final ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation rules and pre-litigation evidence-seeking
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who commit infringement are obliged to compensate the right owner. Additional compensation may be claimed if reputation suffers due to inferior use/production or improper market launch. Before instituting a compensation proceeding, right owner may ask the court to order the person responsible to submit documentation related to the use of the right to determine evidence or damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision allows obtaining business records/evidence prior to filing substantive compensation claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to calculate loss of revenue (damages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Loss of revenue can be calculated per right owner's choice by one of: (a) potential revenue the right owner would have gained absent the infringing competition; (b) the net revenue obtained by the infringer; (c) the license fee that would have been paid if the infringer had used the right under a lawful license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damage includes both actual loss and loss of revenue; right owner selects the calculation method.
